the-life-crime-and-capture-of-john-wilke: Written within months of Lincoln's assassination, George Alfred Townsend's book is the first full account of the crime and the manhunt. Drawing on his work as a war correspondent, Townsend traces Booth's plot, the murder at Ford's Theatre, and the desperate chase through Maryland and Virginia. History written while the shock was still fresh.
god-s-answers-a-record-of-miss-annie-mac: Clara Lowe records the remarkable charity of Annie Macpherson, who rescued thousands of destitute London children and found them homes in Canada. Told through answered prayers and transformed lives, the book is both testimony and history. A moving account of Victorian philanthropy at its most dedicated.
my-lady-of-the-north: Randall Parrish — master of the historical romance — sets this tale of love and adventure in the northern borderlands. His heroine faces danger and divided loyalties with spirit. Parrish's swift, colorful storytelling made him a favorite of readers who loved romance with their history.
keineth: Jane Abbott's novel for young readers follows Keineth through the adventures and lessons of growing up. Friendship, family, and doing the right thing shape a story told with warmth and simplicity. A gentle period piece from the golden age of children's series fiction.
the-rangers-or-the-tory-s-daughter-a-tal: Daniel Pierce Thompson's Revolutionary romance follows the Rangers of the northern frontier — and the Tory's daughter caught between love and loyalty. Set in Vermont's Green Mountains, it blends history with thrilling adventure. A classic of early American historical fiction, full of period spirit.
the-winning-of-barbara-worth: Harold Bell Wright's bestselling novel follows the winning of Barbara Worth — and the winning of the desert itself through irrigation — in early California. Romance and reclamation blend in a story that celebrated hard work and vision. The hugely popular book that made Wright one of America's best-loved authors.
louis-agassiz-as-a-teacher-illustrative-: Lane Cooper collects stories and sayings that show how Louis Agassiz — the great naturalist — taught. His famous method was simple: put the thing itself before the student and make him look, hard, until he truly saw. Teachers of every subject will find wisdom in these pages.
gone-to-earth: Mary Webb's passionate novel of Shropshire follows Hazel Woodus, a wild child of the woods, torn between the love of two very different men. Her devotion to the half-tame fox cub Cubby mirrors her own untamed heart. When the world closes in, her tragedy unfolds with the force of nature itself. A moving, earthy masterpiece from one of England's most gifted regional writers.
the-emigrant-mechanic-and-other-tales-in: Thomas Cowherd, a Canadian blacksmith-poet, rhymes tales of emigrant life with songs of the new land. His homely verse speaks for the working settlers. A genuine folk voice from pioneer Ontario. Anvil, farm, and forest ring through the rhymes of this true poet of the people.
egyptian-tales-translated-from-the-papyr: Flinders Petrie, the father of Egyptian archaeology, translates tales from papyri of the IVth to XIIth dynasties — shipwrecked sailors, clever magicians, and ancient kings. These are among the oldest stories ever written down. The very fountainhead of storytelling, four thousand years old.
trials-and-triumphs-of-faith: Mary Cole recounts trials and triumphs of faith — true stories of humble believers tested by sorrow and delivered by grace. Her earnest narratives comforted many Victorian readers. Simple, sincere Christian testimony, warmly told. Sickbeds, losses, and answered prayers fill these earnest pages.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abbey-of-arbr: This 1913 Catholic Encyclopedia article on the Abbey of Arbroath — the Scottish house of the Declaration of Arbroath — recounts its royal founding and fame. Oswald Hunter-Blair tells its stirring story. A key reference on Scotland's history. Scotland's nobles sealed their famous letter in its chapter house.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-adam-of-murim: This 1913 reference article on Adam of Murimuth — the English chronicler of Edward III's wars. Thomas Walsh follows his annals. Crecy and Calais march through his pages. A canon's view of chivalry's age. His chronicle aids historians still. His work continues Murimuth's earlier chronicle.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-adelard-of-ba: A 1913 entry on Adelard of Bath — the scholar who brought Euclid to the West. William Turner honors his translations. He learned from Arab masters in Spain. England's first man of science. His Euclid taught for centuries. His Quaestiones naturales asked daring questions.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-aelnoth: This 1913 reference piece on Aelnoth — the Canterbury monk who wrote St. Canute's life. Bernard Ward notes his Danish history. He served kings with his pen. The entry preserves his modest fame. A monk among chroniclers. His Canute vita shaped the Danish chronicles.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-aldfrith: A 1913 Catholic Encyclopedia entry on Aldfrith — the learned king of Northumbria. John Joseph A'Becket praises his scholarship. He sheltered Bede's teachers and monks. The Irish called him Flann Fina. A king among scholars. His reign was Northumbria's golden age. Bede praised his wise rule.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-anathoth: A 1913 Catholic Encyclopedia entry on Anathoth — Jeremiah's hometown. Edward Arbez tells its story. The prophet's foes plotted in its streets. Its fields were bought as a sign. A village in Judah's tale. Its ruins lie north of Jerusalem. Abiathar was exiled to its fields.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-articles-of-f: This 1913 reference piece on the articles of faith — the truths the Church proposes. John Wynne sets out their binding force. The creeds sum their number. The faithful assent with divine faith. The charter of Catholic belief. Their denial is the heretic's mark.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-aseneth: A 1913 entry on Aseneth — the wife of Joseph in Egypt. A.E. Breen tells her scriptural story. Pharaoh gave her to the dreamer. Her sons became the tribes. A matriarch of the Egyptian sojourn. Her story inspired the ancient romances.
